findings.description: The `pup merge` entry says "Operator-only, `--pr` included: the verdict moves another session's branch (decisions 26, 44)". That is now false for the conductor tier, because decision 75 lets the conductor run `--pr`; `--approved-by` is also undocumented.
findings.body:
**Stale CLI reference.** This PR lets a `PUP_CONDUCTOR` caller run `pup merge <s> --pr`. The CLI now refuses the conductor only on the local fast-forward (`conductor && !opts.pr`). But `docs/02-cli.md` still describes the whole command as operator-only, `--pr` included:

> Operator-only, `--pr` included: the verdict moves another session's branch (decisions 26, 44).

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/e536243e8ed7b8573523c577bca911e0bc5a0318/docs/02-cli.md#L182-L182

Two more gaps:
- The new `--approved-by <who>` flag is missing from the `--accept-debt` description. The flag is required from the conductor and defaults to `human` for the operator.
- L150 of the same file still says the conductor "is refused `pup merge`", which needs the same `--pr` qualifier.

The PR does not touch `docs/02-cli.md`, so a reader of the CLI reference will conclude the conductor cannot gate (decision 75).
findings.suggestion: - `pup merge <session>` — run the gate pipeline; on pass, merge and write knowledge layer in the same transaction; on fail, move to rejected and inject the report. A session is refused it, `--pr` included: the verdict moves another session's branch (decisions 26, 44). The conductor may run it only with `--pr`, which never moves main, and must pass `--approved-by <who>` with `--accept-debt`; the operator's approver defaults to `human` (decision 75).

findings.description: When the conductor's `--pr` gate is refused for flagged debt, the hint says to re-run with only `--accept-debt "<reason>" --review-by "<condition>"`. Followed as written, that re-run is refused again for a missing `--approved-by`. The same hint text is in `src/core/merge-gate.service.ts` ~L420.

`hasOpenLedgerEntry` includes `accepted_by` in its dedupe key, and that value can now vary. A `--pr` retry after a partial failure (gh died after the push) with a different approver writes duplicate open ledger entries for the same debt. Two examples: the conductor's `tg:alexis` followed by the operator's default `human`, or `tg:Alexis` vs `tg:alexis`.

Nothing stops the conductor from passing `--approved-by human`, or a look-alike with zero-width characters that `sanitizeReason` keeps. The entry then can't be told apart from the operator's own acceptance, which weakens decision 75's goal of attributing approval truthfully. Refusing `human` from the conductor, or requiring a `<channel>:<name>` shape, would close it.

Decision 75 narrows decision 47, which still reads "it is refused `merge`, …". Decision 47 carries no `*Amended by decision 75:*` note, though the file uses that convention elsewhere (e.g. `*Amended by decision 72:*`).
The comment "Only the operator reaches this line without an approver" restates what the conductor guard above already guarantees, and what `approvedBy ?? 'human'` already shows. Consider deleting it.

refuted_findings.description: A conductor can now pass `--gate-env` on `pup merge --pr`. That widens a gate child's environment, which decision 36 reserved for the operator, and can hand the conductor's peer-channel credentials or secrets like GH_TOKEN to test code the session wrote.
refuted_findings.refutation: Decision 36 draws its line between an explicit flag and ambient env (direnv, CI, wrappers), not between callers, and a conductor-typed `--gate-env` is still an explicit flag. The conductor could already pass `--gate-env` to `pup init` and `pup audit`, which refuse only sessions (decisions 48, 64). Decision 47 also gives the conductor unsandboxed Bash in the main checkout, so it can already run a session's code with its whole environment. Gating with `--gate-env` is the more contained path, so the change grants no new capability.

refuted_findings.description: The sentence that every dashboard key 'runs a command that is operator-only somewhere (decisions 42, 44, 47)' needs a decision 75 qualifier now that merge is partly conductor-reachable.
refuted_findings.refutation: The sentence is still true. `m` runs `pup merge --pr`, which is still refused to a session (the 'somewhere'). `u` and `R` are still refused to the conductor. `uiReadOnlyReason` is unchanged, so the dashboard stays read-only for both tiers, as the sentence says.
